data.name: Aqsaht
data.gender_notes: Aqsaht is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Means 'Close to the Sacred House' in Arabic. This name is derived from the name of the second holiest site in Islam, the Al-Masjid Al-Haram in Mecca. It is a powerful and evocative name that suggests a deep connection to the spiritual and sacred aspects of life. The name Aqsaht carries the meaning “Close to the Sacred House” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Aqsaht usually hope their child will grow to embody close to the sacred house and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes a deep connection to the divine and a commitment to living a spiritual life. It is a name that inspires courage, strength, and resilience in the face of life's challenges.
data.etymology: Aqsaht belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Close to the Sacred House.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aqsaht total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

It is a name with historical and religious connections to the second holiest site in Islam, the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem. The name is often used to express a sense of belonging and pride in one's Islamic heritage. It also reflects the importance of the connection between Islam and the people of the Arab and Islamic world to the holy sites of their faith.
data.spiritual_significance: At its core, the Islamic name "Aqsaht" is deeply spiritual in nature. It is a name that symbolizes a deep connection to the sacred and holy places of Islam. For Muslims, the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem represents a place of spiritual refuge and pilgrimage, and the name "Aqsaht" serves as a constant reminder of this connection. The name also represents a reminder of the importance of faith, devotion, and the commitment to uphold the teachings and values of Islam in daily life.
